name: v2.0.0
body:
The major release that modernizes Freelens internals and unlocks further development.

v2.0.0 is a full internal rewrite of how Freelens is built, bundled, and tested. The application, its internal packages, and the extension API are now ESM-first, compiled by a single [Vite](https://vite.dev/) (electron-vite) pipeline directly from TypeScript sources, and tested with [Vitest](https://vitest.dev/). The UI runs on React 19, and the extension API has been redesigned as a specified, frozen contract, checked by porting real extensions to it. Most of the work is in the foundation, but the release also brings a standalone terminal, faster and more reliable cluster connections over HTTP/2, custom resources for users who may not list their definitions, verified binary downloads, and a long list of fixes. The extension API is **not compatible with v1 extensions**.

## What's new:

### Breaking Changes

* The extension API has been reorganized and is **not compatible with Freelens v1 extensions**. Extensions must be updated for v2 before they will load. Extensions may now be authored as either ESM or CommonJS, and must target React 19. See the [migration guide](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/blob/main/docs/extensions/migrating-from-v1.md). See #2102, #2110, #2304, #2465
* Extensions are now installed under the application data directory (`<userData>/extensions`) instead of `~/.freelens/extensions`. Extensions installed for v1 are not migrated and have to be installed again in their v2 versions. See #2400, #2467
* Renderer extensions get no guarantee of Node or Electron, `require()` included; Node work belongs in the main process, reached over IPC. See #2483, #2484
* Freelens is now ESM-first throughout — the main process, the renderer, all internal modules, and the extension API ship as ES modules. See #2102, #1718
* macOS 13 Ventura or later is required: Electron 44 no longer supports macOS 12. See #2864
* Removed the hierarchical-namespaces (HNC) tree view from the namespace details, together with the deprecated `@mui/lab` it was built on. See #2290
* Downloaded kubectl versions start at Kubernetes 1.22, and the China package mirror option is gone (the mirror stopped syncing). Older clusters use the bundled kubectl. See #2348, #2351

### New Features

* Open a terminal outside a cluster session: a standalone terminal page with its own tabs, reachable from the Welcome page, the Catalog, the hotbar and the command palette. It uses your own shell environment, `KUBECONFIG` and `kubectl`/`helm`, and the application's proxy as `HTTPS_PROXY`. See #2359, #2364
* Custom resources work for users who may list them but not their `CustomResourceDefinitions`: the sidebar, the list views and the details are built from the cluster's API discovery instead. See #2675, #2676, #2677, #2679
* Resource search matches across dashes and underscores, so `nginxingress` finds `nginx-ingress`. See #1937, #2711
* Cluster settings to skip the namespace authorization and metrics endpoint checks, for faster connection to large clusters. See #1699
* Terminal tabs show startup progress, including the kubectl download and its verification, instead of a stalled "Connecting ...". See #2357, #2358, #2367, #2368
* macOS natural text editing shortcuts in the embedded terminal (Option+Arrow word navigation, Command+Arrow line navigation, Command/Option+Delete). See #1051, #2338, #2354, #2355
* Installing an extension that is already installed and enabled offers to replace it, or to reinstall the same version, instead of failing with "Disable or uninstall it first". See #2798, #2799
* The Extensions page shows "Failed to load" for an enabled extension whose code did not load, with the process, the stage and the error in its tooltip, and labels each install as `verified`, `unverified` or `development` in colour. See #2780, #2787, #2788
* Downloaded log files have a timestamp in their name, so repeated downloads no longer overwrite each other. See #1884, #2565
* The Node Group column of the nodes list recognizes kops instance groups. See #2454
* The installers have their own icon, the application icon with an install badge, so they are no longer mistaken for the application. See #2838
* The HTTP Proxy preference accepts `socks5://` proxies as well as `http://` and `https://`, and becomes `HTTPS_PROXY` in the terminal outside clusters, as the proxy of a cluster already is in its terminal. Both proxy settings now say what goes through them. See #2433, #2878

### Extensions API

* **A specified contract.** The v2 API is described by normative contracts — the guarantee, the stable surface and the failure mode of each part — and everything it exports stays frozen until the next major. See [api.md](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/blob/main/docs/extensions/api.md), [binaries.md](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/blob/main/docs/extensions/binaries.md) and the [migration guide](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens/blob/main/docs/extensions/migrating-from-v1.md) with the v1 → v2 rename table. See #2304, #2465, #2501, #2562
* **Proven by porting real extensions.** The contract and the migration guide were checked by porting the example, Gateway API, Flux CD, AI, Karpenter, Velero and Freelens for Claude extensions to v2, and every gap found on the way was fixed in the host or in the documentation. The documentation points to [freelens-example-extension](https://github.com/freelensapp/freelens-example-extension) as the reference template, and to its agent skills for creating and porting an extension. See #2653, #2654, #2655, #2662, #2663, #2664, #2665, #2666, #2686, #2687, #2694, #2696, #2705, #2706, #2719, #2723, #2732, #2761, #2770
* **New delivery mechanism.** A built-in installer replaces pnpm (and drops 20 MB of it from every build): install from a package name, a URL, a `.tgz` file or a local directory, with integrity checked at install time. Extensions are served over a privileged `freelens-extension://` scheme and loaded by URL, and a development extension reloads when it is rebuilt — once per rebuild, also for a build that writes its main and renderer entries in two runs. Installing from a typed Windows drive path now works. See #2400, #2467, #2468, #2469, #2471, #2472, #2500, #2710
* **Host singletons.** React, ReactDOM, the JSX runtime, MobX, mobx-react and Monaco are shared with extensions through the `FreelensExtensionApi` global, so an extension never ships its own copy. `@ogre-tools/*` is no longer part of the contract; an extension that wants dependency injection bundles its own. See #2450, #2474, #2534, #2535
* **Complete Kubernetes types.** `K8sApi` re-exports the whole kube-object and kube-api type surfaces, and `KubeApi` and the other type-and-value pairs can be named as types again. The concrete host store classes are no longer exported. See #2365, #2475, #2478, #2480, #2504, #2505
* **Typed registrations.** `Renderer.K8sApi.detailsFor()` and `menuItemFor()` build detail and menu registrations from the model class, so a component written for another kind does not compile. Pages, preference inputs and hints, menu items and cluster frame components are typed with the props the host actually passes. See #2655, #2656, #2670, #2671, #2672, #2692
* **Custom resources.** A new `customResources` field lists the custom resources an extension presents with pages of its own, and hides them from the Custom Resources tree of the sidebar while the extension is enabled. The host registers an API and a store for every served version of a CRD, prefers the served storage version, and drops the APIs and stores of a deleted CRD. See #2655, #2656, #2668, #2674, #2698, #2700
* **The host's kubectl, helm and terminal environment** are available to main-process extensions through `Main.Shell`: the binaries Freelens runs for a cluster, with the download and verification phases reported, and the environment its terminals get. The same code now prepares the cluster, node shell and standalone terminals. See #2704, #2709, #2712, #2715
* **Renderer-safe utilities.** `Main.Util.fetch`, the host's proxy-aware `fetch`, typed as the standard `fetch` (the renderer uses Chromium's global `fetch`), `createReactKey`, `sha256Hex` and `kustomizeHash` hashing helpers, a Node-free event emitter for `CatalogCategory`, and the Node-bound members removed from `Util`. `Catalog.getAllClusters()` and `getClusterById()` are observable by contract in both processes. See #2395, #2396, #2481, #2482, #2487, #2488, #2489, #2490, #2723, #2732
* **Fixes found by the ports.** `KubeJsonApi.forCluster` is callable, `objectConstructor` of an API object is the class itself, so a store over a host API applies its watch events, `ExtensionStore` accepts a model declared as an interface, disabling an extension stops the sync of its stores instead of leaving two copies saving each other in an endless loop, stylesheets load without console errors, and `Renderer.Navigation.navigate` warns about a relative pathname. An unset boolean query value of `KubeApi` (`follow`, `watch`, `previous`, `timestamps`) is no longer sent as `true`, and `PodApi.deleteWithFinalizers()` really clears the finalizers. See #2651, #2652, #2667, #2669, #2707, #2708, #2721, #2722, #2759, #2767, #2770
* **A leaner published package.** `@freelensapp/extensions` ships a self-contained declaration built with TypeScript 7 and rolldown-plugin-dts. Unused members that pulled Electron, `react-window`, `@xterm/xterm`, MUI, `forRemoteCluster` and several abandoned packages into the declaration are gone, every external package it imports is declared, and the build fails if it ever references Node. See #2360, #2363, #2375, #2388, #2445, #2446, #2485, #2486, #2498, #2499, #2545, #2557, #2559
* An in-repo fixture extension tests the contract in the unit and integration suites on all three platforms. See #2451, #2452, #2492, #2500

### Architecture

* **Vite replaces webpack.** The entire webpack setup — the app bundle, the `packages/core` library bundle, and the infrastructure build — is replaced by a single electron-vite pipeline for the main, preload, and renderer processes. See #2102, #2112, #2118
* **Single transpilation from TypeScript source.** Every workspace package is now consumed directly from its TypeScript sources; no package emits a `dist/` bundle. The separate transpilation shims that repackaged ESM-only dependencies are gone. See #2102, #2113
* **Vitest replaces Jest.** The 33 per-package Jest configurations and the whole layer of ESM-in-CommonJS workarounds (`ts-jest`, the custom resolver, `@side/jest-runtime`) are replaced by one root Vitest configuration running on the same Vite pipeline as the app. The suites run through a single sharded Vitest invocation with CI-friendly reporters. See #2102, #2109, #2123, #2185, #2595
* **Separate runtime environments in type-checking.** Main, renderer and common code are type-checked against their own runtime (Node without DOM, DOM without Node), so an API the process does not have fails the build. See #2491, #2492, #2493
* **React 19 and in-house routing.** React was upgraded from 17 to 19 in staged steps, with `React.StrictMode` enabled in development, ref-as-prop, `react-window` v2 and the deprecated mobx-react `disposeOnUnmount` replaced. The `react-router` v5 / `history` v4 stack was replaced by an in-house router in `@freelensapp/routing`, with the used parts of `path-to-regexp` v1 and `history` v5 vendored in. See #2154, #2251, #2254, #2261, #2263, #2266, #2267, #2268, #2269, #2270, #2278, #2280, #2283, #2286, #2289, #2298, #2393
* **Per-process HTTP.** `node-fetch` is gone: the renderer uses Chromium's fetch and the main process uses undici. `http-proxy-node16` was replaced by the maintained `http-proxy-3`. See #2361, #2373, #2540, #2541
* **Proxies named after what they are.** The two proxies of the main process are now `FreelensProxy`, which serves the renderer, and `FreelensK8sProxy`, the per-cluster `freelens-k8s-proxy` process, and their log lines carry `[FREELENS-PROXY]` and `[FREELENS-K8S-PROXY]`. See #2572, #2573, #2829
* **Dependency and toolchain cleanup.** Dropped `electron-rebuild` and `node-gyp` in favor of `node-pty` prebuilds, removed the `@freelensapp/legacy-global-di` package, unified the build patterns across executable packages, moved shared versions into a pinned pnpm catalog, unified `tsconfig` on the ES2025 baseline, switched to the React automatic JSX runtime, moved `electron` to `devDependencies`, re-enabled `knip` (now also for unused files and stylesheets), and switched Node.js builtin imports to the `node:` prefix. See #2126, #2128, #2129, #2131, #2137, #2164, #2228, #2229, #2247, #2125, #2330, #2336, #2678
* **Fewer, lighter dependencies.** Several third-party libraries were replaced with native APIs or lighter, maintained equivalents: lodash → [es-toolkit](https://es-toolkit.dev/), moment / moment-timezone → native `Date` and `Intl`, crypto-js → `node:crypto`, query-string → `URLSearchParams`, url-parse → `URL`, grapheme-splitter → `Intl.Segmenter`, semver → [verkit](https://www.npmjs.com/package/verkit), p-limit → es-toolkit `limitAsync`, react-beautiful-dnd → [@dnd-kit](https://dndkit.com/), react-table → an in-house sortable table, and `stoppable`, `typed-regex`, `typed-emitter`, `glob-to-regexp`, `randomcolor` and `winston-transport-browserconsole` → small in-house code. `mobx-react-lite` is gone in favour of `mobx-react` alone. `selfsigned` was upgraded to v5, Chart.js from v2 to v4, MUI from v5 to v9, and `@ogre-tools/*` from 17 to 27. See #2167, #2306, #2180, #2188, #2189, #2217, #2197, #2394, #2386, #2387, #2389, #2390, #2391, #2392, #2220, #2177, #2282, #2316, #2326, #2178, #2618, #2620, #2630, #2632, #2807

### Improvements

* Cluster requests travel over HTTP/2 end to end: the internal proxy serves the renderer over HTTP/2, and talks HTTP/2 to the per-cluster `freelens-k8s-proxy` too, so all requests of a cluster share one connection. A cluster view with many open watches no longer stalls its other requests behind Chromium's six-connection limit, and list views close their watch requests when you leave them. See #2444, #2566, #2568, #2569, #2570, #2784, #2820, #2830
* Cluster requests recover when the k8s proxy process exits on its own, instead of failing with "connection refused" until the cluster is reconnected. Concurrent requests no longer spawn duplicate proxy processes, a proxy that cannot start answers at once with the reason instead of hanging, and its restarts are bounded. A change of the server address in the kubeconfig is picked up, and the proxy of a cluster removed from the catalog is stopped, as is every proxy on quit. See #2563, #2564, #2713, #2714, #2716, #2717, #2718, #2720, #2789, #2791
* Authentication failures back off (1 minute, then 5 minutes, then pause until you reconnect) instead of running an exec credential plugin such as kubelogin every 30 seconds and opening a browser tab each time. A failing connection also reports its error 16 seconds sooner. See #2459, #2629, #2634
* Watch events are applied with one index per flush, and a list is sorted again only when a field it is sorted by changed, which makes busy clusters with thousands of objects cheaper to follow. See #2783, #2792, #2793
* Cluster CPU and memory charts keep their history on clusters with node churn (Karpenter, Cluster Autoscaler, spot instances). See #2456
* The logs tab no longer freezes for seconds with "Show timestamps" on, and stale pod log requests are cancelled instead of piling up. See #2463, #2494
* Freelens no longer fills `~/.kube/cache/discovery` with an entry for every session: kubectl, helm and the cluster terminals get a cache directory of their own for the proxy kubeconfig. See #2437, #2649, #2650
* Shell sync no longer runs the Electron binary as Node inside your shell: the environment is read with `env -0`, so multi-line values come through, a shell that hangs is killed together with everything its profile started, and a failure is shown once the window is ready instead of never. See #2724, #2725, #2726, #2727, #2728, #2730
* Windows terminals run on node-pty's bundled, Microsoft-signed ConPTY, and closing a terminal no longer starts a short-lived helper process. See #2729, #2731
* Notifications start below the close button of the Extensions and Preferences pages instead of covering it, and the "Extension successfully installed" notification hides on its own. See #2697, #2699, #2794, #2795, #2854
* Avatar colours are deterministic and always keep a readable contrast with their text. See #2392
* A terminal shows its last output again after the window reloads, kept by the main process, and an edit tab stores only its unsaved changes. API responses are kept out of the HTTP cache, and the caches are cleared on start. See #2872, #2873, #2874
* Simpler, faster development: a single Vite dev server with hot module replacement (`pnpm dev`) and a single build step (`pnpm build:app:dir`) replace the previous multi-stage webpack builds, and both work on Windows, ARM64 included. See #2102, #2118, #2165, #2526, #2810
* Faster, more reliable builds and CI: unchanged binaries are no longer re-downloaded and the integration-tests workflow was sped up across all platforms. See #2213, #2216, #2774
* Documented v2 styling conventions (theme CSS custom properties, global SCSS, CSS Modules, and Tailwind CSS v4) and auto-injected extension stylesheets. The legacy in-house flexbox utilities have been fully migrated to Tailwind and the `flexbox.scss` layer removed. See #2144, #2145, #2162

### Security

* The digests of the bundled `kubectl`, `helm` and `freelens-k8s-proxy` are pinned in a lock file, verified against the publisher's signature (GitHub build provenance, PGP, keyless cosign) at bump time, and every bundled binary is hashed against the lock on every build, including one restored from a cache. Checksum verification is mandatory, including Windows binaries, which were previously never verified. See #2342, #2345, #2346, #2774
* Every kubectl downloaded at runtime is checked against a pinned, signature-verified checksum; a version without a pin is never downloaded. See #2348, #2350, #2351
* The compromised eMudhra intermediate certificates are refused: Electron, since v43.8.3, blocks them in Chromium and in Node's `tls`, `https` and `fetch`, and freelens-k8s-proxy v2.0.0, built with Go 1.27.3, in its connection to the cluster. See #2832
* CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder of Node.js, is fixed by Node v24.22.1 in Electron v44.10.0. The user interface was not affected, because Chromium decodes Brotli with its own, fixed copy. See #2848, #2881
* A security policy describes how to report a vulnerability privately, and which versions are supported. See #2800
* The last release is scanned in its own workflow, and the main branch nightly. See #2340

### Fixes

* Clusters whose API server, or a gateway in front of it, answers with a relative redirect can be opened, instead of failing with `Unexpected token '<'`. See #2757
* Deleting or changing resources from the UI works on clusters behind a gateway that refuses unknown origins, such as the GitLab agent, instead of failing with a 403 and "Unknown error occurred while ok-ing". See #2842
* Extensions no longer flip between Enabled and Disabled in a loop after they are installed, freezing the application. See #1005, #2777
* A command sent to a new terminal (Pod Shell, Pod Attach, extensions) is no longer lost when the shell takes more than 10 seconds to start, and a terminal closed while it starts leaves no shell process, or privileged node shell pod, behind. See #2806, #2817, #2818, #2819
* A change of the Terminal Shell Path preference applies to the next terminal of a cluster, without restarting the application. See #2841
* With "Automatically start Freelens on login" enabled, the application starts hidden on macOS 13 and later, as it already did on Windows. See #2864
* The "App crash" page of a page that threw goes away when you navigate elsewhere. See #2808
* Fixed RoleBinding and ClusterRoleBinding dialogs: "Create" did nothing for a new binding, selected service accounts were not shown, and pressing Enter in the Users or Groups field submitted the dialog too early. See #2119, #2458
* A secret value revealed in the pod details no longer stays revealed when switching to another pod, and the details of the new object load their referenced config maps. See #2416, #2457
* The pod context menu closes when a Logs, Shell or Attach submenu item is clicked. See #2043, #2466
* Clicking a path picker button several times no longer opens several file dialogs at once. See #2455
* An aborted list load no longer shows a "Failed to load" warning or leaves a list empty until the window is reloaded. See #2300, #2496, #2527
* The main process no longer crashes when its stdout pipe is closed, for example when launched through Amazon AppStream 2.0. See #2370, #2372
* Ingress rows with many routes no longer push the following rows out of view. See #2195
* Managed fields entries that differ only by subresource are now distinguishable in the details drawer. See #2299
* Wizard dialogs, confirmation dialogs and dialog select menus now follow the dark theme. See #2196, #2257
* Byte-valued chart Y axes no longer force a 1-unit step. See #2191
* Word-wrapped log rows no longer overlap. See #2166
* Disconnecting a cluster no longer logs an error that the application window failed to load. See #2760, #2762
* Helm > Charts shows the charts of a repository added or removed in the preferences without reloading the cluster. See #2867, #2868
* The Install button of a chart with a long name and the Save button of the values of a release stay on screen. See #2851
* Secret values that are not valid base64 are shown as they are, instead of being decoded leniently into wrong data. See #2190

### Updates

* Built with electron-vite 6 on Vite 8, tested with Vitest 5, type-checked with TypeScript 7, and styled with Tailwind CSS v4.
* Runs on React 19.3, MobX 7, MUI 9 and Monaco 0.57, and talks to clusters with `@kubernetes/client-node` 2.0.
* Upgraded to Electron v44 (previously v41 in Freelens v1.10). See #2192, #2198, #2538, #2542, #2863, #2864, #2881
* Over 180 dependency updates in total, including 16 security updates (dompurify, js-yaml, undici, tar, sharp, joi, fast-xml-parser, handlebars, vitest, uuid, pnpm and Electron).
* Uses Electron v44.10.0 with Chromium 152.0.7977.169 and Node v24.22.1
* Has bundled kubectl v1.37.1, Helm v4.3.1 and freelens-k8s-proxy v2.0.0

name: v1.10.3
body:
This is a patch release that adds support for admission policy resources and new Nodes list columns, respects the default-container annotation, and fixes node and pod metrics, cluster loading, cluster events, pod logs, and kubectl binary handling.

## What's new:

### New Features

* Added support for the `ValidatingAdmissionPolicy` and `ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding` resources. See #2089, #1688

### Bug Fixes

* Clusters no longer get stuck on the loading screen when the CRD store subscription fires before the cluster proxy is ready. See #2093, #1617
* Node CPU usage in the Nodes list view is now formatted in cores instead of being rendered as `0.0Ki`. See #2084, #1883
* The "Show previous terminated container" log option is no longer persisted as a global default, so new pod log tabs no longer start with it enabled. See #2096, #2095
* The bundled kubectl binary is no longer removed when its self-check hits a transient `EBUSY` error (e.g. when the file is briefly locked on Windows). See #2063
* The default kubectl download mirror is now used as a fallback when the custom mirror preference is left empty. See #2064
* Prometheus metrics queries no longer fail when `kube_pod_info` exposes duplicate series that differ only by a flapping `pod_ip` / `host_ip` label. See #2086

### Improvements

* The Kubernetes API proxy now supports SOCKS5 proxies for upgrade requests (used by exec, attach, and port-forward), so these features work behind a SOCKS5 proxy. See #2092
* Freelens now respects the `kubectl.kubernetes.io/default-container` annotation: the Attach, Pod Shell, and Pod Logs actions target the annotated container instead of always using the first one, falling back to the first container when the annotation is missing or invalid. See #2098, #1557
* The Nodes list view gained pods, instance type, node group, and capacity columns (hidden by default, sortable and searchable) plus a resource requests overlay, which are especially useful on managed-cloud clusters. See #2097, #1940
* Node memory usage now shows `N/A` instead of `NaN` when metrics-server data is missing. See #2084
* Pod logs now use a light background in the Light theme instead of always rendering dark. See #2019
* Cluster sidebar pages that were previously unreachable from the command palette can now be found there. See #2090, #1782
* Events from the newer `events.k8s.io/v1` API now show their source and repeat count. See #2074
* Kubeconfigs stored on a WSL 9p share are now watched via polling, so newly added clusters appear without restarting Freelens. See #2083
* Prometheus/Thanos query errors are now logged with the actual server error to make failing queries easier to diagnose. See #2085
* The bundled binaries directory is now added to `PATH` in PowerShell and fish terminals, matching the behavior of other shells. See #2062

### Updates

* 17 dependencies have been updated in total.
* Uses Electron v41.10.0 with Chromium 146.0.7680.216 and Node v24.18.0
* Has bundled kubectl v1.36.2 and Helm v4.2.2

name: v1.10.2
body:
This is a patch release containing signed binaries for Windows that should bypass false positive alerts from antivirus programs.

## What's new:

### Bug Fixes

* Fixed extension installs failing when the user-data directory did not contain a `package.json`. See #2016
* Fixed the pod context menu staying open after clicking a sub-menu item. See #2054

### Improvements

* Windows binaries are now signed, which should prevent false-positive alerts from antivirus programs.
* `node-pty` now ships as a prebuilt binary to avoid antivirus false positives in `conpty_console_list.node` (Win64.Trojan.Ulise). See #2023, #2018
* The Helm binary path and the Helm server-side apply preference are now persisted. See #2046

### Updates

* 20 dependencies have been updated in total.
* Uses Electron v41.9.0 with Chromium 146.0.7680.216 and Node v24.17.0
* Has bundled kubectl v1.36.2 and Helm v4.2.2

name: v1.10.1
body:
## What's new:

This is a patch release with fixes and updates for v1.10.0 that couldn't be released as Flatpak because of the issue with the `app.asar` archive.

### Bug Fixes

* Fixed empty lines accumulating below word-wrapped log blocks in the log viewer. See #2006
* Synchronous spawn errors from external binaries (e.g. kubectl, helm) are now reported as failures instead of crashing the app. See #2001

### Improvements

* Reduced packaged app size by excluding cross-platform native binaries at pack time instead of pruning `app.asar`. See #2000
* Release artifacts now include a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM). See #2005

### Updates

* 5 dependencies have been updated in total, including 3 security updates.
* Uses Electron v41.7.2 with Chromium 146.0.7680.216 and Node v24.15.0
* Has bundled kubectl v1.36.2 and Helm v4.2.2

name: v1.10.0
body:
## What's new:

### New Features

* Time range selector for metrics charts — choose from predefined windows (1 h, 3 h, 24 h, 7 d…) or enter a custom start/end time. See #1475, #1962
* Custom download mirror URL for kubectl in Preferences → Kubernetes → Kubectl, useful for air-gapped environments. See #1825
* Pod details now show the scheduler name (e.g. `default-scheduler`). See #1942
* Node details now show the cloud provider ID (e.g. `aws:///us-east-1a/i-...`). See #1926

### Bug Fixes

* Fixed pod status: successfully completed pods and Job pods no longer show a warning icon. See #1913
* Fixed UI freezes on clusters with large numbers of pods. See #1956
* Fixed a crash on clusters with many CRDs installed (Istio, Kyverno, Flux, KEDA, etc.). See #1876
* Fixed "Bad Request" errors when installing Helm charts. See #1897
* Fixed Option-key character combinations in the integrated terminal on macOS with non-US keyboard layouts (`|`, `{`, `}`, etc.). See #1965
* OCI image volumes are now displayed in pod details instead of showing "Unknown pod volume kind". See #1924
* IPv6:Port endpoints are now correctly formatted in the Endpoints listing. See #1838
* Fixed kubectl exec / port-forward / attach when proxying through a bastion (Warpgate, Teleport). See freelensapp/freelens-k8s-proxy#150

### Extensions API

* Expose navigateToPreferences on renderer extension API. See #1983

### Improvements

* Kubeconfig entries added or removed in Preferences now take effect immediately without restarting the app. See #1951
* Log viewer preferences (timestamps, word wrap, show previous container logs) are now persisted globally. See #1904
* Linked search preference is now remembered across restarts. See #1872
* Welcome page is now the first item in the default hotbar on a fresh install. See #1950
* App binaries are now built natively on Ubuntu 24.04, macOS 15, and Windows 11, eliminating spurious "Intel Mac" warnings for Apple Silicon users. See #1868, #1949
* Reduced download size: the macOS DMG is now about 50 MB smaller. See #1966

### Updates

* Upgraded to Electron v41 with Node.js v24 (previously Node v22). See #1833
* 28 dependencies have been updated in total, including 5 security updates.
* Uses Electron v41.7.2 with Chromium 146.0.7680.216 and Node v24.15.0
* Has bundled kubectl v1.36.2 and Helm v4.2.1

name: v1.6.1
body:
Bugfixing release that address the problem on Windows with opening the terminal.

* Removed security patch that broke application on Windows (#1228, #1232)

## Notes from v1.6.0:

Ready for Kubernetes v1.34. New improvements and bug fixes.

* Views for (cluster) role bindings show more details and hyperlinks to (cluster) roles and service accounts. (#1125)
* Added HTTPS support and custom prefix in Prometheus settings. (#1131)
* Pods and other resources can be force deleted or force finalized. (#1147)
* Pods and Deployments lists have some additional columns that are hidden by default. (#1136)
  * New column with pod IP address (hidden by default).
  * New (old) column with number of deployment replicas in `N/N` format (hidden by default).
  * Columns with node and QoS are now hidden by default.
  * More hyperlinks in the details.
* Node list shows Ready/NotReady condition and has a column if the node is schedulable. (#1196, #1207)
* CronJob and Job have a field "Resumed" rather than "Suspend". (#1141)
* Items to the list of allowed namespaces or groups and roles to the bindings can be added from a single comma-separated string. (#1144) 
* Only the first load balancer and the rule of the ingress are shown in the list and more in the tooltip. (#1146, #1217)
* Better compatibility with VictoriaMetrics. (#1111, #1202)
* Paste action works for the search box in the editor, too. (#1216)
* More assertions to prevent crashes. (#1145, #1201)
* Fixed CVE-2025-7783, CVE-2025-54798, CVE-2025-5889 in dependencies. (#1209, #1210, #1211, #1213)
* Updated Electron 35.7.5
* Updated Helm 3.19.0
* Updated kubectl 1.34.1
* 55 other dependencies have been updated in total.
